data.title: What ASML Doubters Overlooked
data.description:
If ASML sat on your watchlist instead of in your portfolio, the gain over the last year may feel like a missed shot. Holding ASML over the past year would have returned 40.9%, including dividends. That outcome raises a sharper question. Back on 20 November 2025, when analysts still argued over how fast EUV and High NA tools might spread, what signals could have helped you judge whether AI driven wafer starts would really justify those bullish adoption assumptions?

ASML has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On ASML

The shares cost €890 at the start of the period. At that point, ASML sat between two very different stories about how deep the AI driven wafer cycle might run and how much lithography spending governments and chipmakers would really commit to.

On the bullish side, one narrative saw a Fair Value of €950, a price implied by expectations that AI, cloud and data center demand would drive EUV and High NA tools, plus service contracts, far beyond prior cycles. That view leaned on an assumption that earnings could reach €13.9b by about 2028 with P/E at 31.6x.

The more cautious script pinned Fair Value at €769, a level based on assumed revenue growth of 7.2% and profit margin of 30.4% over roughly three years. It treated geopolitical risk and export controls as central threats, with tariffs and restrictions on China seen as potential brakes on ASML’s addressable market and High NA adoption.

What The Results Changed For The ASML Thesis

Record Q3 2026 figures gave the bullish ASML story its strongest support. Reported revenue reached €11.7b versus €7.5b a year earlier, and net income moved from €2.1b to €5.0b. Net margin shifted from 28.3% to 42.5%. Management also reported demand for AI related tools that supply cannot fully match. Rising export control risk around China still challenged the upside case, so the evidence cut both ways.

The whole debate turned on how much AI driven lithography demand would show up in actual orders and profitability. For any other chip equipment group, the same check is simple. Track multi quarter revenue, backlog comments and reported net margin against the story being told about AI and wafer starts.

What ASML’s Run Leaves You Paying For Today

ASML now trades at €1,168 after a 40.9% gain over the past year, and this Narrative’s Fair Value view sits below that level. The gap reflects concern that today’s quote already charges a premium for ASML’s position in advanced lithography.

According to Thomas_Regrettier, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, the crux for anyone buying at today’s price is whether ASML can keep its geopolitical exposure contained while remaining the dominant supplier of leading edge tools to a very small group of customers.

"ASML’s story is one of quiet dominance at the heart of global tech. Founded in the Netherlands in 1984, ASML started as a joint venture between Philips and ASM International. Over the decades, it evolved into the sole supplier in the world of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which are essential for manufacturing the most advanced semiconductor chips (like those powering AI, smartphones, and data centers)."

data.title: Is It Smart To Buy Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) Before It Goes Ex-Dividend?
data.description:
Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) stock is about to trade ex-dividend in three days. The ex-dividend date is usually set to be one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date on which you must be present on the company's books as a shareholder in order to receive the dividend. The ex-dividend date is important because any transaction on a stock needs to have been settled before the record date in order to be eligible for a dividend. Therefore, if you purchase Xylem's shares on or after the 24th of November, you won't be eligible to receive the dividend, when it is paid on the 22nd of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.43 per share. Last year, in total, the company distributed US$1.72 to shareholders. Last year's total dividend payments show that Xylem has a trailing yield of 1.8% on the current share price of US$95.24. Dividends are a major contributor to investment returns for long term holders, but only if the dividend continues to be paid. So we need to check whether the dividend payments are covered, and if earnings are growing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are typically paid out of company income, so if a company pays out more than it earned, its dividend is usually at a higher risk of being cut. That's why it's good to see Xylem paying out a modest 37% of its earnings. A useful secondary check can be to evaluate whether Xylem generated enough free cash flow to afford its dividend. Fortunately, it paid out only 44% of its free cash flow in the past year.

It's positive to see that Xylem's dividend is covered by both profits and cash flow, since this is generally a sign that the dividend is sustainable, and a lower payout ratio usually suggests a greater margin of safety before the dividend gets cut.

Check out our latest analysis for Xylem

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Companies with consistently growing earnings per share generally make the best dividend stocks, as they usually find it easier to grow dividends per share. If business enters a downturn and the dividend is cut, the company could see its value fall precipitously. It's encouraging to see Xylem has grown its earnings rapidly, up 27% a year for the past five years. Earnings per share have been growing very quickly, and the company is paying out a relatively low percentage of its profit and cash flow. Companies with growing earnings and low payout ratios are often the best long-term dividend stocks, as the company can both grow its earnings and increase the percentage of earnings that it pays out, essentially multiplying the dividend.

Another key way to measure a company's dividend prospects is by measuring its historical rate of dividend growth. Xylem has delivered an average of 11% per year annual increase in its dividend, based on the past 10 years of dividend payments. Both per-share earnings and dividends have both been growing rapidly in recent times, which is great to see.

The Bottom Line

Is Xylem an attractive dividend stock, or better left on the shelf? We love that Xylem is growing earnings per share while simultaneously paying out a low percentage of both its earnings and cash flow. These characteristics suggest the company is reinvesting in growing its business, while the conservative payout ratio also implies a reduced risk of the dividend being cut in the future. It's a promising combination that should mark this company worthy of closer attention.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Moog

Notably, that recent sale by Non-Executive Chairman John Scannell was not the only time they sold Moog shares this year. data.title: 3 Trade Reset Stocks With Real Exposure to UK EU Food Flows
data.description:
The UK and EU just hit reset on trade, and that could quietly reshape how food, agriculture and logistics stocks linked to cross border flows are valued over the next few years. Friction at the border has trapped plenty of potential, and easing checks might release it. This article walks through three stocks exposed to that story, why the news matters to them, and what informed investors may want to watch next.

The three stocks below are just a sample of the idea, while the full screen surfaced 19 more UK and EU food, agriculture and logistics companies with equally compelling stories that are not covered here. STEF (ENXTPA:STF)

Overview: STEF runs temperature controlled transport and logistics for fresh, frozen and chilled food across Europe, linking producers, retailers and food service.

Operations: Most revenue comes from STEF France at about €2.6b, with STEF International contributing roughly €2.1b and other activities about €0.8b.

Market Cap: €1.6b

STEF sits right in the UK–EU trade re integration theme, moving chilled and frozen food through the cold chain that SPS checks directly affect. A P/E around 12.5x and rising sales in recent results provide some context for that exposure. What matters now is how pressure on the cost of keeping food cold and moving affects future pricing power.

If you want to see whether that pricing power story is already baked in, start with the DCF valuation analysis for STEF to see what the market might be missing.

Cranswick (LSE:CWK)

Overview: Cranswick is a UK pork, poultry and prepared foods producer supplying chilled and ready to eat products to retailers, food service and export markets.

Operations: Cranswick generates about £2.9b from Food and £47.6 million from Other, with £2.9b in the UK and modest Continental Europe and Rest of World sales.

Market Cap: £3.0b

For the UK–EU trade re integration theme, Cranswick matters because it ships chilled pork and poultry into retailers and restaurants that rely on predictable border processes. DKDGI, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote an in depth view on the stock, argues that what looks like a steady compounder story still hides a few pressure points investors should not ignore.

"Risks: heavy investment years push the payout to 60-70% of free cash flow after leases; animal disease; dependence on major UK grocers."

Future returns for Cranswick could hinge on how one unseen cost pressure interacts with those chunky capex cycles and already committed cash flows.

That hidden pressure point is where things get interesting, and the full narrative for Cranswick shows how Cranswick’s reinvestment cycle and cash commitments could be quietly decoupling from headline stability.

Südzucker (XTRA:SZU)

Overview: Südzucker is a large European food group anchored in sugar and ingredients, supplying major food, beverage and industrial customers across the UK and wider continent.

Operations: Südzucker generates about €2.9b from Sugar, €2.3b from Special Products, €1.7b from Fruit, €1.0b from Starch and €906 million from CropEnergies.

Market Cap: €2.2b

For the UK–EU trade re integration theme, Südzucker matters because smoother agri food flows can tighten sugar supply chains, as the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St highlights a turning point in how the sugar cycle might feed into pricing and profitability.
